answer: Each agent deposits a falcon‑sized bond on the mesa of the network, recorded in the Atlas ledger; the bond is locked for a challenge window. When a new identity appears, neighboring nodes audit its recent signatures and, if a majority detects a duplicate key, they broadcast a slashing proof that instantly forfeits the bond. The attacker therefore pays the full bond amount per fake identity, typically a multi‑thousand‑token stake, plus the opportunity cost of the lock‑up period.
